diagnostic_evidence.quote: I_y &\lesssim h^4 \int_{\HH} \left\{ \sum_{k=0}^4 \left(x_2^{k-3} \partial_{x_2}^k v(\x)\right)^2 + \sum_{k=0}^2 \left(x_2^{k-2}\partial_{x_1}\partial_{x_2}^k v(\x)\right)^2 + h^2  \sum_{k=0}^4 \left(x_2^{k-4} \partial_{x_2}^k v(\x)\right)^2 \right\} \dd{\x}

&\lesssim h^4 \int_{\HH} \left[(x_2 \partial^3_{x_1}v(\x))^2  + (x_2 \partial^2_{x_1}\partial_{x_2} v(\x))^2 + h^2 (\partial^3_{x_1}v(\x))^2+ h^2 (\partial^2_{x_1}\partial_{x_2} v(\x))^2 + (x_2^2\partial^4_{x_1} v(\x))^2\right]\dd{\mu(\x)}.

issues.failure_explanation: The I_y portion of the proof culminates in the bound eq:estimate-first-lapl-Iy, which is written (and correctly derived) with respect to Lebesgue measure \dd{\x}. The theorem's constant C^v, however, is built from \|\cdot\|_{{\rm L}^2(\HH)} norms, i.e. with respect to the hyperbolic measure d\mu = x_2^{-2}dx_1dx_2 (as explicitly fixed in Hypothesis hyp:biserica-Grivitei, and as is correctly done in the companion I_x estimate eq:estimate-first-lapl-Ix, which ends with \dd{\mu(\x)}). Since \int (x_2^p \partial^k v)^2 dx = \|x_2^{p+1}\partial^k v\|^2_{L^2(\HH)}, the proven I_y bound is h^4 times \|x_2^{k-2}\partial_{x_2}^k v\|^2 + \|x_2^{k-1}\partial_{x_1}\partial_{x_2}^k v\|^2 + h^2\|x_2^{k-3}\partial_{x_2}^k v\|^2 in hyperbolic norms — one power of x_2 more in every I_y sum than the stated C^v. Hence the final inference "The conclusion follows by ..." is not justified: the displayed estimates do not imply the stated bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Raise each I_y-related x_2 exponent in C^v by one power: \sum_{k=0}^4 \|x_2^{k-2}\partial_{x_2}^k v\|, \sum_{k=0}^2 \|x_2^{k-1}\partial_{x_1}\partial_{x_2}^k v\| and h\sum_{k=0}^4 \|x_2^{k-3}\partial_{x_2}^k v\|. This is exactly what the proof's own Lebesgue-measure display eq:estimate-first-lapl-Iy yields via dx = x_2^2 d\mu; the corrected C^v remains \mathcal{M}_\gamma-controlled, so the \mathcal{O}(h^2) rate and every downstream conclusion are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:consistency-first-lapl is not established with its explicit constant C^v. The same C^v is imported by rem:1-lapl-bounded-domain and feeds the final consistency statement rem:consistency-first-laplace-sos for the first operator; the abstract convergence results thm:added-1 and thm:convergence-theta are affected only through this instantiation. All of these survive the repair, since the corrected C^v is still controlled by \|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{M}_\gamma}.
issues.title: First-Laplacian consistency constant C^v uses hyperbolic L^2 norms, but the derived I_y estimate is in Lebesgue measure, so every I_y x_2-weight in C^v is one power too small
issues.why_classification: The repair merely aligns the stated constant with what the proof already computes (an immediate measure conversion, no new argument); the method, the O(h^2) rate, the M_gamma-controlled constant, and all advertised downstream guarantees survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Write W = v/x_2^2. Because the projection of the vertical neighbours carries the weight ((j\pm1)^2-1/4), the vertical part of the consistency error is \int_{C} [((j+1)^2-1/4)W(x_2+h) + ((j-1)^2-1/4)W(x_2-h) - 2(j^2-1/4)W(x_2) - \partial^2_{x_2}v] dx. Expanding ((j\pm1)^2-1/4) = (j^2-1/4) \pm 2j + 1 and \partial^2_{x_2}v = x_2^2\partial^2_{x_2}W + 4x_2\partial_{x_2}W + 2W, this equals \int_C [(j^2-1/4)(W^+ + W^- - 2W) + 2j(W^+ - W^-) - x_2^2\partial^2_{x_2}W - 4x_2\partial_{x_2}W] dx + \int_C [W^+ + W^- - 2W] dx. The proof's I_y identity keeps exactly the first integral and omits \int_C [W(x_2+h)+W(x_2-h)-2W(x_2)] dx. That term is a genuine second difference of size h^2\partial^2_{x_2}W; its contribution to Err_h(v) is of order h^2(\|\partial^2_{x_2}v\|_{L^2(\HH)} + \|x_2^{-1}\partial_{x_2}v\| + \|x_2^{-2}v\|), i.e. precisely the order being proved, so the displayed identity is false and the dropped term is not negligible (it also cannot be absorbed into the zero-mean trick, which uses the exact weight j^2-1/4).

failure_location.quote: I_y = \sum_{i \in \Z, j \geq 2} \left(j^2 -\frac{1}{4}\right) & \left\{  \int_{\CC^{i,j}_h} \left\{  \left(j^2 -\frac{1}{4}\right)\left[ \frac{v(x_1,x_2\pm h)}{(x_2\pm h)^2} - \dfrac{v(x_1, x_2)}{x_2^2}\right] - x_2^2 \partial^2_{x_2} \left[\frac{v(x_1,x_2)}{x_2^2}\right] \right.\right.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the term \int_C [W(x_2+h)+W(x_2-h)-2W] dx in the expansion and estimate it by Taylor's formula and Cauchy-Schwarz, exactly as for the other remainders: \sum_j (j^2-1/4)(\int_C \Delta_2 W dx)^2 \lesssim h^4 \int x_2^4 (\partial^2_{x_2}W)^2 d\mu \lesssim h^4 (\|\partial^2_{x_2}v\|^2 + \|x_2^{-1}\partial_{x_2}v\|^2 + \|x_2^{-2}v\|^2), adding these (still \mathcal{M}_\gamma-controlled) norms to C^v; they are automatically covered once the exponents of C^v are corrected as in ISSUE-001.
issues.overall_effect: The consistency proof for \Delta_h^{(1)} contains a false identity, so Theorem thm:consistency-first-lapl's estimate is not established as written; the downstream consistency statements rem:1-lapl-bounded-domain and rem:consistency-first-laplace-sos (and hence the application of the abstract convergence theorems to the first operator) inherit the gap until repaired.
issues.title: Vertical expansion in the first Laplacian's consistency proof drops the second-difference term produced by ((j\pm 1)^2-1/4) = (j^2-1/4) \pm 2j + 1
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local, routine Taylor/Cauchy-Schwarz estimate using only tools already in the paper; no new lemma or construction is needed and the O(h^2) rate, the M_gamma-controlled constant, and every downstream guarantee survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The extra boundary error of the restricted operator comes from the missing neighbours, i.e. from the terms (j^2-1/4)(\Pi_h v) evaluated on the first layer of cells outside the index range (columns i = \pm(N+1), row j = M+1). Since N = \lfloor D/h \rfloor gives Nh \leq D < (N+1)h, the column N+1 = [Nh+h/2, Nh+3h/2] overlaps the interior of \HHD by up to h/2; since M = \lfloor (D-1/D)/h \rfloor + 1 gives Mh as low as D-1/D, the row M+1 can lie entirely below D (by up to 1/D - h/2). The resulting boundary mass is of order (D/h)^2 \|v\| over those cells, but the cells are not contained in \HH\setminus\HHD as the remark states (for \gamma < 1 the domain \HHD is even strictly contained in \mathbb{H}^2_{2/(5h)}, so the two strip-tail terms do not cover the boundary cells either). For example, for \gamma<1 and a smooth v supported in the strip D-1/D < x_2 < D, |x_1| < D, all four tail terms vanish while the boundary error is nonzero and exceeds C_v h^2 by a factor that blows up as h \to 0. The same defect affects the analogous unlabelled bounded-domain consistency remark for \Delta_h^{(2)} in Section 5.3, whose outside layers i=\pm(N+1), j=\pm(M+1) likewise protrude inside \HHD.

failure_location.quote: \|\Delta^{(1)}_{h,D} \Pi_{h,D} v - \Pi_{h,D} \Delta_g v\|_{\ell_{h,D}^2} \leq  C_v\, h^2 & + C\left[\frac{D^2}{h^2}  \|v(x)\|_{{\rm L}^2(\HH\setminus \HHD)}+ \|\Delta_g v(x)\|_{{\rm L}^2(\HH\setminus\HHD)} \right.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the tails over \HH\setminus\mathbb{H}^2_{D'} with D' slightly smaller than D (e.g. D' = D-2h for the lateral strips and D' = D-1/D-2h for the top strip, or uniformly D' = D - c(h + 1/D)). Lemma lem:tail-control applies verbatim to D' = \zeta' h^{-\gamma} with \zeta' \to \zeta, so the final consistency remarks keep exactly their stated form.
issues.overall_effect: The bounded-domain consistency estimates as stated are false for admissible v. The final h^2 consistency remarks rem:consistency-first-laplace-sos and rem:consistency-second-laplace-sos, and therefore the instantiation of the abstract convergence theorems thm:added-1 and thm:convergence-theta for both discrete Laplacians, depend on them; all of these survive the repair with the same conclusions and constants.
issues.title: Bounded-domain consistency tails do not cover the outside-neighbour cells that protrude inside the computational domain
issues.why_classification: The repair widens the tail region by an O(h)/O(1/D) strip and reuses the existing tail lemma with an adjusted constant; it is short, local, and routine, and every advertised conclusion, rate, and regime is preserved.
